controls.title: REST API user enumeration limited
controls.description: The WordPress REST API must not unnecessarily expose user accounts to unauthenticated visitors.
controls.rationale: Public user enumeration supports targeted attacks and broken access control scenarios.
controls.recommended_value: REST endpoints do not unnecessarily expose user accounts.

controls.title: Open user registration reviewed
controls.description: Open user registration must be disabled unless explicitly required for the site.
controls.rationale: Unrestricted registration expands the attack surface and access control scope.
controls.recommended_value: User registration is disabled or justified and restricted.

controls.title: Privileged accounts limited
controls.description: Administrator accounts must follow least-privilege practices and be limited to authorized personnel.
controls.rationale: Excessive privileged accounts increase the impact of credential compromise.
controls.manual_review_instructions: Review administrator accounts, shared credentials, and role assignments; remove unnecessary privileges.

controls.title: HTTPS and TLS configured
controls.description: The WordPress site must be configured to use HTTPS for all public traffic.
controls.rationale: Transport encryption protects data in transit against interception and cryptographic failure.
controls.recommended_value: Site URL and Home URL use HTTPS.

controls.title: Sensitive URL parameters excluded from analytics
controls.description: Sensitive query parameters must not be transmitted to third-party analytics providers.
controls.rationale: Analytics payloads can leak credentials, tokens, and personal data outside the security boundary.
controls.recommended_value: Configured sensitive query parameters are excluded from analytics.

controls.title: Form input handling reviewed
controls.description: Forms that accept user input must use validated, sanitized handling appropriate to the data collected.
controls.rationale: Unvalidated input is a primary vector for injection and cross-site scripting.
controls.manual_review_instructions: Review form plugins and custom handlers for input validation, sanitization, and output escaping.

controls.title: Database query protections verified
controls.description: Custom database queries must use parameterized APIs rather than concatenated SQL.
controls.rationale: SQL injection remains a critical risk when custom queries bypass WordPress database APIs.
controls.manual_review_instructions: Review custom themes, plugins, and snippets for direct SQL usage; confirm $wpdb->prepare() or ORM equivalents are used.

controls.title: Third-party integrations inventoried
controls.description: Third-party scripts, forms, and services with site access must be inventoried and reviewed.
controls.rationale: Insecure design often begins with unreviewed third-party dependencies and data flows.
controls.recommended_value: Personal-data forms and third-party integrations are listed for review.

controls.title: Security requirements documented for integrations
controls.description: Security requirements for new plugins, themes, and integrations must be documented before deployment.
controls.rationale: Documented security expectations reduce insecure-by-default design decisions.
controls.manual_review_instructions: Document security review criteria for plugin, theme, and integration changes before production deployment.

controls.title: Debug mode disabled in production
controls.description: WordPress debug mode must be disabled on production sites.
controls.rationale: Debug output can expose paths, queries, and configuration details to attackers.
controls.recommended_value: WP_DEBUG is false or undefined in production.

controls.title: Theme and plugin file editor disabled
controls.description: The WordPress theme and plugin file editor must be disabled in production.
controls.rationale: In-admin file editing allows rapid compromise if an administrator session is hijacked.
controls.recommended_value: DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT is enabled or the file editor is otherwise disabled.

controls.title: Default administrator username avoided
controls.description: The default "admin" username must not be used for privileged accounts.
controls.rationale: Predictable usernames simplify credential-guessing and brute-force attacks.
controls.recommended_value: No active account uses the default "admin" username.

controls.title: WordPress core on supported version
controls.description: WordPress core must be maintained at a supported version with security updates applied.
controls.rationale: Outdated core components are a common source of exploitable vulnerabilities.

controls.title: Plugin inventory maintained
controls.description: Installed plugins must be inventoried to support patch and vulnerability management.
controls.rationale: Component visibility is required to identify and remediate vulnerable plugins.
controls.recommended_value: Installed plugins are inventoried for review.

controls.title: Unused plugins deactivated
controls.description: Plugins that are not required for site operation should be deactivated and removed when possible.
controls.rationale: Inactive but installed plugins still expand the attack surface.
controls.manual_review_instructions: Review inactive plugins and remove those no longer required.

controls.title: Authentication configuration reviewed
controls.description: Authentication settings including registration and login exposure must be reviewed.
controls.rationale: Misconfigured authentication expands account creation and credential attack opportunities.
controls.recommended_value: Authentication and registration settings are reviewed and justified.

controls.title: Multi-factor authentication for administrators
controls.description: Multi-factor authentication should be enforced for WordPress administrator accounts.
controls.rationale: MFA significantly reduces account takeover risk for privileged users.
controls.manual_review_instructions: Confirm MFA is enabled for all administrator accounts through your identity or security plugin.

controls.title: Password and session policies documented
controls.description: Password strength, rotation, and session timeout requirements must be documented and enforced where feasible.
controls.rationale: Weak credential and session policies increase authentication failure risk.
controls.manual_review_instructions: Document password policies, MFA requirements, and session timeout settings for WordPress access.

controls.title: Plugin and theme sources verified
controls.description: Plugins and themes must be installed only from trusted sources such as WordPress.org or verified vendors.
controls.rationale: Untrusted components can introduce malware or backdoors that compromise integrity.
controls.owasp_reference: A08:2025 Software and Data Integrity Failures
controls.manual_review_instructions: Review installed plugins and themes; confirm they were obtained from trusted sources and have not been tampered with.

controls.title: Update integrity controls reviewed
controls.description: Automatic and manual update processes must preserve software integrity.
controls.rationale: Compromised update channels can inject malicious code into production systems.
controls.owasp_reference: A08:2025 Software and Data Integrity Failures
controls.manual_review_instructions: Document how core, plugin, and theme updates are tested and applied, including rollback procedures.

controls.title: Security event logging enabled
controls.description: Security-relevant events such as authentication and administrative actions must be logged and retained.
controls.rationale: Logging supports detection, investigation, and response to security incidents.
controls.owasp_reference: A09:2025 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
controls.manual_review_instructions: Confirm security logs are retained and reviewed for WordPress admin, authentication, and hosting events.

controls.title: Administrator activity log available
controls.description: Administrative actions affecting compliance posture must be recorded in an audit trail.
controls.rationale: Activity logs support accountability and post-incident investigation.
controls.owasp_reference: A09:2025 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
controls.recommended_value: ComplyOps administrator activity log is available.

controls.title: Continuous compliance monitoring scheduled
controls.description: Automated compliance monitoring must run on a defined schedule when continuous monitoring is in use.
controls.rationale: Scheduled audits detect configuration drift and emerging control deficiencies.
controls.owasp_reference: A09:2025 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
controls.recommended_value: ComplyOps monitoring interval is set to daily, weekly, or monthly.

controls.title: Outbound HTTP request controls reviewed
controls.description: Outbound HTTP requests initiated by WordPress or plugins must be reviewed for SSRF risk.
controls.rationale: Server-side request forgery can expose internal services through WordPress HTTP APIs.
controls.manual_review_instructions: Review plugins and custom code that fetch remote URLs; restrict allowed hosts and validate user-supplied URLs.

controls.title: Private content leakage reviewed
controls.description: Private content must not leak through REST, uploads or caching.
controls.rationale: Broken access control includes unintended disclosure.

controls.title: WordPress checksum integrity
controls.description: WordPress core integrity should be verifiable through checksums.
controls.rationale: Supply chain failures include unexpected core modifications.

controls.title: Unexpected executables in uploads
controls.description: Upload directories must not contain unexpected executable files.
controls.rationale: Supply chain and integrity failures often manifest as web shells.

controls.title: Rate limiting or login protection
controls.description: Rate limiting or login protection should be present for abuse-prone flows.
controls.rationale: Insecure design includes missing anti-automation controls.

controls.title: Session timeout reviewed
controls.description: Administrative sessions should expire within an acceptable interval.
controls.rationale: Authentication failures include weak session management.

controls.title: Trusted update sources
controls.description: Plugin and theme updates should come from trusted sources with modifications restricted.
controls.rationale: Software and data integrity depends on trusted update channels.
controls.owasp_reference: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

controls.title: Repeated server errors monitored
controls.description: Repeated HTTP 500 responses should be monitored and investigated.
controls.rationale: Mishandled exceptional conditions can leak data or weaken security.

controls.title: Failed scheduled tasks reviewed
controls.description: Failed cron jobs and integration failures should be reviewed.
controls.rationale: Operational failures can break security controls silently.

controls.title: Outbound request controls
controls.description: Outbound request controls should limit SSRF-style abuse from WordPress.
controls.rationale: SSRF remains a relevant WordPress risk even outside the 2025 Top Ten list.

controls.title: Security headers present
controls.description: HSTS, framing protection and referrer policy should be present where applicable.
controls.rationale: Security misconfiguration includes missing transport and browser protections.

controls.title: HTTP Strict Transport Security enabled
controls.description: HSTS should be configured to enforce HTTPS for returning visitors.
controls.rationale: Missing HSTS allows downgrade attacks on subsequent connections.

label: OWASP Top 10:2025 WordPress Profile
disclaimer: Technical readiness profile only; not an OWASP certification.
